title: 2D and 3D Shapes: Flat and Solid Shapes
seo_title: Kindergarten Shapes Worksheets: 2D and 3D Shapes, Sides and Corners
standard_text: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten shapes worksheets: name circles, squares, triangles, rectangles and hexagons, name cubes, spheres, cones and cylinders, tell flat from solid, count sides and corners, and find shapes around us. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count sides and corners to name a flat shape. Solid shapes take up space.
key_sub: Size and turn do not change a shape’s name. A ball is a sphere, a can is a cylinder.
body_html:
Flat shapes

Flat shapes lie flat on paper. Count the sides and corners to name them.

ShapeSidesCorners
Circle00
Triangle33
Square4 (all the same)4
Rectangle44
Hexagon66

Solid shapes

Solid shapes take up space. You can hold them.

ShapeLike a…
Cubenumber cube
Sphereball
Coneparty hat
Cylindercan

Size and turn do not matter

A big triangle and a small triangle are both triangles. A turned square is still a square.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Calling a turned square a diamondCount the sides: 4 equal sides is a square
Mixing up circle and sphereA circle is flat. A sphere is solid
Mixing up square and rectangleA square has 4 sides of the same length

faq.q: What shapes should a kindergartner know?
faq.a: Flat shapes: circle, square, triangle, rectangle and hexagon. Solid shapes: cube, sphere, cone and cylinder.

faq.q: What is the difference between 2D and 3D shapes?
faq.a: 2D shapes are flat, like a drawing on paper. 3D shapes are solid and take up space, like a ball or a box.

faq.q: Is a turned square called a diamond?
faq.a: It is still a square. Turning a shape does not change its name. Count the sides and check that they are the same length.

faq.q: How can I practice shapes at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt: find circles (plates), rectangles (doors), cylinders (cans) and spheres (balls). Ask how many sides and corners each flat shape has.
